Hypertension is one of the most common chronic conditions encountered in
primary care, affecting a substantial proportion of the adult population
worldwide. It is defined as a persistent elevation of arterial blood pressure
above accepted thresholds, and is a major modifiable risk factor for
cardiovascular disease, stroke, and chronic kidney disease.

First-line pharmacologic management often includes ACE inhibitors such as
lisinopril, which reduce blood pressure by decreasing the production of
angiotensin II. Lifestyle modification, including dietary sodium restriction
and regular physical activity, remains an important adjunct to pharmacologic
therapy.

Type 2 diabetes mellitus frequently coexists with hypertension and shares
overlapping cardiovascular risk. Metformin remains the preferred initial
agent for glycemic control in most patients, given its favorable safety
profile and evidence of cardiovascular benefit.
